title: Session prioritizer fuzzy rulebook
body:
Purpose:
- Brain dump / working spec for a lightweight, fuzzy-rule-based session prioritizer service that sits in ingress and influences routing/batching decisions.
- Goal: let product teams express soft preferences (latency vs cost vs freshness) per-session/tenant without rewriting routing logic.

High-level goals / constraints:
- Config-first: express rules in simple JSON/YAML that map to a score modifier.
- Runtime: evaluate O(10-50) rules per request, sub-ms evaluation cost, deterministic ordering fallback.
- Safety: low risk—rules only tweak priorities (score delta), they cannot evict or kill requests.
- Integrations: should surface to Console (per-route) and be pluggable for Dedicated/Private.

Quick sketch of how it fits the stack (ASCII):

ingress-proxy ---> ingress-router ---> session-prioritizer ---> batcher ---> serving-runtime
                                 |                                 ^
                                 |-> metrics / debug / trace ----|

- ingress-router: picks model + route, applies static route policy.
- session-prioritizer: applies fuzzy rulebook to compute session_score (float). Router uses session_score to:
  * pick priority lane (hot/warm/cold)
  * bump prewarming / cache hints
  * set batching weight (smaller batch weight => lower latency)

API surface (draft):
- POST /v1/prioritize
  request: { session_id, tenant, route, metadata, hinted_slo_ms, cost_sensitivity, freshness_hint }
  response: { score: float, lane: string, annotations: [string], rule_ids_applied: [string] }

- GET /v1/rulebook (admin): returns compiled rules + stats
- PUT /v1/rulebook (admin): upload JSON/YAML ruleset (validated)
- POST /v1/eval-preview (admin): simulate a batch of sessions and get effects

Config model (fuzzy rules) - minimal viable schema (JSON-ish):

[
  {
    "id": "rush-hour-tenant-bump",
    "priority": 20,
    "condition": {
      "all": [
        {"equals": {"tenant": "acme"}},
        {"in_time_range": {"start": "17:00", "end": "19:00", "tz": "UTC"}}
      ]
    },
    "action": {
      "score_delta": 0.45,
      "lane": "hot",
      "ttl_seconds": 60
    },
    "notes": "bump acme sessions during peak for better latency"
  }
]
Core condition operators (minimal): equals, in_set, regex, lt, gt, in_time_range, percent_rollout (randomized), header_contains
Action fields: score_delta (float, additive), set_lane (optional), batching_weight_multiplier (0.5-2.0), prewarm_hint (bool), annotate (string)

Evaluation semantics (proposal):
- Evaluate rules in ascending priority (lowest number first) but last-wins for lane if multiple set it.
- score starts at base_score = route_default_score. Each rule adds score_delta. Final score clipped to [0.0, 1.0].
- percent_rollout evaluates using deterministic hash(session_id, rule_id) < rollout_percent.
- ttl_seconds on action to avoid flapping; we issue a session-level sticky override in local memcache keyed by session_id if rule has ttl.

Example: inferred request /v1/prioritize body:
{
  "session_id": "s_34a2",
  "tenant": "acme",
  "route": "text-generate-ec2-low-latency",
  "metadata": { "client_version": "1.2.4", "device_class": "mobile" },
  "hinted_slo_ms": 150,
  "cost_sensitivity": 0.2,
  "freshness_hint": 0.8
}

Sample response (conceptual):
{
  "score": 0.78,
  "lane": "hot",
  "annotations": ["rush-hour-tenant-bump","mobile-latency-boost"],
  "rule_ids_applied": ["rush-hour-tenant-bump","mobile-latency-boost"]
}

Why fuzzy rules vs DSL or ML policy:
- Pros: transparent, editable, debuggable, low infra cost, easy canary via percent_rollout.
- Cons: may be noisy when many tenants create overlapping rules; need good observability.

Observability / debug needs:
- per-rule hit counters, percent of sessions affected, average delta on latency/cost (approx), P50/P95 of resulting lane latency.
- evaluation trace: for a session, list rules evaluated, branching decisions, final score. Flag rules that consistently degrade SLO.
- dashboard: heatmap of tenant vs lane distribution over time.

Safety and rollout plan:
- default-off for tenant-level rules. Admins enable per-tenant after trial.
- sandbox mode: rulebook can be uploaded to experiment namespace and previewed with /v1/eval-preview before applying.
- emergency kill switch: global toggle to set all score_delta=0 and respect only base_score.

Performance considerations:
- ruleset size: aim < 1000 rules per cluster node. Use compiled rule trie for quick equals/in_set checks.
- caching: memoize session_id->score for ttl_seconds. Use LRU with small footprint per node.
- deterministic evaluation order to make debugging reproducible.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent composite scoring for multi-objective (latency*alpha + cost*(1-alpha))? Do we compute a single scalar or return multi-dim hints?
- Should the service emit recommended batching_weight or should router translate score->lane->batching? (Prefer router map but allow explicit weight).
- Policy conflict resolution: propose simple last-wins with explicit priority and an admin validation step that warns on overlap.
- Do we allow tenant-uploaded rules or require managed templates? Security review needed.
- Serialization format: YAML for humans + compact compiled binary for runtime.

Notes to self / action items:
- spike: implement evaluator + microbench (Go) and benchmark 1000 rules, 1M reqs/s synthetic. (Assign Arjun)
- Console: add "preview" UI to paste rule and simulate (Lena)
- Add example rule templates: mobile-latency-boost, low-cost-background, realtime-trade-priority
- Draft RFC for infra: cache design + kill-switch + audit logs.

References / related tickets:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prioritizer/pull/128 (early evaluator impl)
- JIRA-5173: ingress prioritization spike
- Slack thread: #ingress-heuristics (link above)

Quick curl example for QA (local dev):
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/prioritize -d '{"session_id":"s-test","tenant":"acme","route":"text-gen"}'

Rough timeline:
- 2w spike: evaluator + perf tests + simple rulebook format
- 3w: integrate with router, add memcache sticky overrides, basic metrics
- 2w: console preview + admin APIs + canary for specific tenant

Personal notes: keep this lightweight. Start with additive float score only. If we need finer control, extend to return multi-dim hints later. Try to avoid too many condition operators initially—focus on equals, in_set, in_time_range, percent_rollout.

End of scratch/brain dump.

(If revisiting: capture a few recorded example sessions and trace their final lane distribution to validate defaults.)
